sources.authors: Collins, G. S.; Melosh, H. J.; Marcus, R. A.
sources.title: Earth Impact Effects Program: A Web-based computer program for calculating the regional environmental consequences of a meteoroid impact on Earth
sources.notes: Issue 6. doi.org resolves to onlinelibrary.wiley.com (Wiley returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch). Metadata (title, 3 authors, vol 40, issue 6, pp. 817-840, June 2005) confirmed via Crossref REST API. Full text read from the author-hosted journal-formatted PDF linked from the official calculator page (impact.ese.ic.ac.uk/static/effects.pdf, PDF pp. 1-24 = journal pp. 817-840). Every equation transcribed from rendered page images, not only from text extraction (text layer garbles Greek letters and radicals).

sources.authors: Collins, G. S.; Lynch, E.; McAdam, R.; Davison, T. M.
sources.title: A numerical assessment of simple airblast models of impact airbursts
sources.notes: Issue 8; CC-BY 4.0. Metadata confirmed via Crossref REST API; full text (Early View pagination 1-19) read from Imperial College Spiral repository. The section 'The Earth Impact Effects Program' (EV p. 15 = journal p. 1556) documents three changes to the web calculator; Eq. 7 transcribed from rendered page image. Linked from the official calculator page as 'Recent improvements in the airblast calculation'.

sources.authors: Collins, G. S.; Melosh, H. J.
sources.title: Errata and Improvements in Earth Impact Effects Program (technical note dated May 13, 2013)
sources.container: Appended (PDF pp. 25-30) to effects.pdf distributed with the Impact: Earth! calculator
sources.notes: NOT peer-reviewed: author note documenting software changes (Eq. 4 and Eq. 20 typo corrections, length-of-day, complex-crater depth d_fr = 0.294 D_fr^0.301, tsunami rim/collapse waves). Read in full from rendered page images. Cites Wunnemann, Collins & Weiss 2010 (Rev. Geophys. 48, RG4006, doi 10.1029/2009RG000308; bibliographic data confirmed via Crossref only, full text not opened, no values taken from it).

sources.authors: Marcus, R. A.; Melosh, H. J.; Collins, G. S.
sources.title: Impact: Earth! web calculator (Purdue University build; client-side bundle static/js/main.a4859e04.js)
sources.notes: Year = access date (2026-10-04); build date unknown. The physics is computed in the browser; the bundle was downloaded and its calculation functions executed verbatim in Node.js; the live page was also driven in a browser for cases A, B, C and displayed identical (rounded) values. Used as the primary oracle.

sources.authors: Collins, G. S.; Melosh, H. J.; Marcus, R. A.
sources.title: Impact: Earth! / Earth Impact Effects Program web calculator (Imperial College London server; gunicorn; results at /map)
sources.notes: Year = access date (2026-10-04). Form posts by GET to https://impact.ese.ic.ac.uk/map (fields documented in 07-eiep.md sec. 7.1). In 'distance only' mode the page prints energy, entry, airblast and crater sections only (no thermal, seismic or ejecta text); thermal/seismic/ejecta enter only as map-circle radii (radians) in inline JavaScript. Old URLs (ImpactEarth/cgi-bin/*.cgi, lpl.arizona.edu/impacteffects) now 404 or redirect.

parameters.label: Energia kinetyczna impaktora
parameters.notes: rho_i [kg m^-3] impactor density; L0 [m] diameter at top of atmosphere; v0 [m s^-1] velocity at top of atmosphere. Exact for a sphere (non-relativistic). Program actually uses relativistic KE (only matters near c). Calculators report this as 'Energy before atmospheric entry'.

parameters.label: Rozkład liczebności NEA
parameters.notes: L_km [km]. Not starred = not implemented. Source: NASA NEO Science Definition Team 2003 (report, not opened).

parameters.label: Interwał powrotu (cała Ziemia)
parameters.notes: E_Mt = E/(4.18e15 J). Assumes collision probability ~1.6e-9 /yr per object. Both online calculators now use a different law (max(piecewise-in-mass, 110 E_Mt^0.77)) - see disagreements.

parameters.label: Interwał powrotu w promieniu r
parameters.value: T_RL = T_RE / (2 (1 - cos Delta))   [errata 2013 form; printed 2005 form: T_RL = (T_RE/2)(1 - cos Delta)]
parameters.locator: Eq. 4*, p. 819; errata note Eq. (1), p. 1
parameters.notes: Delta = r/R_E [rad]. Geometric area fraction of a spherical cap is (1 - cos Delta)/2, which gives T_RL = 2 T_RE/(1 - cos Delta); neither the printed nor the 'corrected' form equals this (errata form is 4x smaller). Not needed for the 24-h simulation.

parameters.label: Atmosfera wykładnicza
parameters.notes: rho0 = 1 kg m^-3 (surface), H = 8 km (scale height), z [m] altitude. Earth curvature and gravity ignored; straight trajectory.

parameters.label: Równanie oporu
parameters.value: dv/dt = -3 rho(z) C_D v^2 / (4 rho_i L0)
parameters.notes: C_D = 2. Ablation and gravity ignored.

parameters.label: Opór względem wysokości
parameters.value: d(ln v)/dz = 3 rho(z) C_D / (4 rho_i L0 sin(theta))
parameters.notes: Uses dt = -dz/(v sin theta); theta = trajectory angle to horizontal.

parameters.label: Prędkość przed fragmentacją
parameters.value: v(z) = v0 exp(-3 rho(z) C_D H / (4 rho_i L0 sin(theta)))
parameters.notes: Used for intact impactors (I_f >= 1) and up to breakup altitude z*. If v at surface < terminal velocity, max of the two is used.

parameters.label: Wytrzymałość a gęstość
parameters.notes: rho_i [kg m^-3]; Y_i yield strength [Pa]. Valid ~1000-8000 kg m^-3. Gives ~130 Pa at rho=0. (Text layer of the PDF drops the square root; image shows sqrt.)

parameters.label: Warunek fragmentacji
parameters.notes: Transcendental; not solved directly in the program.

parameters.label: Wysokość rozpadu
parameters.notes: v_i here = entry velocity v0 [m s^-1]; H = 8000 m; rho0 = 1 kg m^-3. Valid only if I_f < 1.

parameters.label: Czynnik nienaruszenia I_f
parameters.value: I_f = 4.07 C_D H Y_i / (rho_i L0 v_i^2 sin(theta))
parameters.notes: I_f >= 1: impactor reaches surface intact. Purdue code uses an effective coefficient 2.7185*0.75 = 2.039 instead of 4.07 (see disagreements); irrelevant for km-size impactors (I_f ~1e-6).

parameters.label: Rozpłaszczanie (model naleśnikowy) w czasie
parameters.value: d^2L/dt^2 = C_D P_s/(rho_i L) = C_D rho(z) v(z)^2/(rho_i L)
parameters.notes: Initial condition L = L0 at z = z*.

parameters.label: Rozpłaszczanie względem wysokości
parameters.notes: Valid if L changes little over H (Chyba et al. 1993).

parameters.label: Średnica roju fragmentów L(z)
parameters.notes: Used at z = 0 for strewn-field size (calculators: 'ellipse' L(0)/sin(theta) by L(0)).

parameters.label: Prędkość po rozpadzie
parameters.value: v(z) = v(z*) exp( -(3/4) (C_D rho(z*) / (rho_i L0^3 sin(theta))) * Integral_z^z* exp((z* - z')/H) L(z')^2 dz' )
parameters.notes: Velocity drops as a double exponential after breakup. Integral closed forms: Eq. 19 (airburst) or Eq. 20 (to ground).

parameters.label: Wysokość eksplozji powietrznej
parameters.notes: f_p = 7 (pancake factor; paper notes physically 2-4, Chyba et al. 5-10). z_b > 0: airburst; z_b <= 0: swarm hits ground (crater-forming). Negative z_b is unphysical; the Purdue code clamps it to 0, the Imperial server apparently does not (affects airblast; see disagreements).

parameters.label: Całka dla eksplozji powietrznej
parameters.value: Int_{z_b}^{z*} exp((z* - z)/H) L^2 dz = (l L0^2/24) alpha [8(3 + alpha^2) + 3 alpha (l/H)(2 + alpha^2)],  alpha = sqrt(f_p^2 - 1)

parameters.label: Całka do powierzchni (errata)
parameters.locator: Eq. 20, p. 821; corrected in errata note Eq. (2), p. 1
parameters.notes: Printed 2005 form has a typo ('34 + (l/H)^2'); use the errata form. Purdue code implements the errata form.

parameters.label: Hamowanie w warstwie wody
parameters.value: v_seafloor = v_surface exp(-3 rho_w C_D d_w / (2 rho_i L sin(theta)))
parameters.notes: rho_w = 1000 kg m^-3; C_D = 0.877 (rigid sphere, supersonic, Landau & Lifshitz); d_w [m] water depth; L [m] diameter after atmosphere. Then: water-layer transient crater uses Eq. 21 with 1.365 and rho_t = 1000 and v_surface; seafloor crater uses v_seafloor and rho_t = 2700 (paper; Purdue code uses 2750). Airblast and thermal use E_surface; seismic and ejecta use E_seafloor. No tsunami in 2005 version.

parameters.label: Średnica krateru przejściowego
parameters.notes: D_tc at pre-impact surface [m]; L [m] after atmospheric traverse; v_i [m s^-1] at surface; g_E [m s^-2]; theta to horizontal. Gravity regime, solid rock. Constant uncertain: best estimate within 0.8-1.5. Calculator code effectively uses 1.16132 (1.6 (pi/6)^(1/3) 1.61^-0.22).

parameters.label: Krater przejściowy w wodzie
parameters.notes: rho_w = 1000 kg m^-3; v_i = velocity at water surface.

parameters.label: Krater prosty – średnica
parameters.notes: Applied if D_tc <= 2.56 km.

parameters.label: Objętość soczewki brekcji
parameters.notes: Unbulked breccia lens.

parameters.label: Głębokość krateru przejściowego
parameters.notes: Code uses D_tc/2.828.

parameters.label: Krater złożony – średnica
parameters.notes: D_tc, D_fr, D_c in km (dimensionally homogeneous, so m works too); D_c = 3.2 km (simple-complex transition on Earth). Applied if D_tc > 2.56 km (i.e. 1.25 D_tc > D_c). Not quoted if D_tc > 1500 km (melt province).

parameters.label: Głębokość krateru złożonego (2005, zastąpione)
parameters.notes: D_fr, d_fr in km. SUPERSEDED by errata note Eq. (9); neither online calculator uses it any more.

parameters.label: Głębokość krateru złożonego (2013)
parameters.method: scaling:lunar d/D 1.04 D^0.301 divided by 0.7 g_Earth/g_Moon (~3.5)
parameters.notes: D_fr, d_fr in km; in metres: d_fr = 36.76 D_fr^0.301 (code: 37 D^0.301). Implemented by both calculators. Non-peer-reviewed note.

parameters.label: Objętość stopu (ogólna)
parameters.notes: eps_m = 5.2 MJ kg^-1 (granite); V_i impactor volume. Valid v_i > ~12 km/s, comparable densities, vertical impacts.

parameters.label: Objętość stopu (program)
parameters.notes: E [J] impact energy at surface (seafloor for marine). Assumes rho_i = rho_t = 2700. ~10x larger for ice; underestimates for very large impacts (geotherm ignored); overestimates by ~2 for theta <= 15 deg.

parameters.label: Grubość pokrywy stopu
parameters.notes: Crater floor ~ transient crater diameter (Croft 1985). Calculators print this value while saying 'roughly half the melt remains in the crater'.

parameters.label: Objętość wyrzutów i wału
parameters.notes: Paraboloid transient crater, depth/diameter 1/(2 sqrt 2).

parameters.label: Średnica krateru przejściowego na grzbiecie wału
Objętość krateru przejściowego
parameters.notes: Equating V_e = V_tc gives h_tr = D_tc/14.1. Purdue code uses pi/24 D_tc^3 for the Vtc/V_Earth ratio.

parameters.label: Wysokość wału krateru końcowego
parameters.notes: Text says 'Equation 31' - typo for Eq. 47.

parameters.label: Promień kuli ognistej
parameters.method: yield scaling:R_f = 13 L0 at 20 km/s, 2700 kg/m3
parameters.notes: E [J]. Radius at time of max radiation (transparency temperature reached). Simulations give 10-15 L0; 13 adopted. Only if v_i >= 15 km/s.

parameters.label: Ekspozycja cieplna
parameters.notes: eta = 3e-3 (luminous efficiency; literature range 1e-4 to 1e-2, Ortiz et al. 2000); r [m] distance along surface. Multiplied by f (Eq. 36). Neglects weather/atmospheric absorption ('upper estimate').

parameters.label: Czas napromieniowania
parameters.value: tau_t = eta E / (2 pi R_f*^2 sigma T*^4)
parameters.notes: sigma = 5.67e-8 W m^-2 K^-4; T* = 3000 K (air transparency 2000-3000 K).

parameters.label: Ułamek kuli ognistej nad horyzontem
parameters.notes: If h >= R_f*: f = 0 (fireball below horizon, no direct radiation). Refraction/extinction near horizon ignored.

parameters.label: Wysokość ukryta za horyzontem
parameters.notes: Delta = r/R_E [rad]. R_E not given numerically in paper (code: 6370 km).

parameters.label: Próg zapłonu (fizyka)
parameters.value: Phi_ignition ~ T_ignition rho c_p sqrt(kappa tau_t)
parameters.notes: Explains E^(1/6) scaling; not used directly.

parameters.label: Skalowanie progu zapłonu
parameters.notes: Thresholds at 1 Mt in Table 1 (see thresholds).

parameters.label: Magnituda sejsmiczna
parameters.method: Gutenberg-Richter energy relation with seismic efficiency 1e-4
parameters.notes: E [J] impact energy (seafloor energy for marine). Seismic efficiency 1e-4 (range 1e-5 to 1e-3, Schultz & Gault 1975) is built into the constant; a factor 10 in efficiency shifts M by 0.67.

parameters.label: Magnituda efektywna (r < 60 km)
parameters.notes: r_km = distance in KILOMETRES; valid r_km < 60.

parameters.label: Magnituda efektywna (60–700 km)
parameters.notes: r_km in KILOMETRES; valid 60 <= r_km < 700. Jump vs 41a at 60 km: -0.024.

parameters.label: Magnituda efektywna (r ≥ 700 km)
parameters.notes: Delta = epicentral angle in RADIANS (Delta = r/R_E, defined p. 819 and Fig. 1 caption; NOT degrees, NOT km). Confirmed by Purdue code (log10(r_km/6370)) and by the Imperial server's MMI-IV map radius (reproduces M to 1e-5 only with radians). Valid r_km >= 700. Discontinuity at 700 km: 41b gives M - 4.524, 41c gives M - 4.807 (jump -0.28). With degrees the jump would be ~3.2 magnitudes.

parameters.label: Czas dotarcia wstrząsów
parameters.notes: r_km in km; surface-wave speed ~5 km s^-1 (upper crust).

parameters.label: Grubość wyrzutów (ogólna)
parameters.notes: Exponent -3 (range -2.5 to -3.5); r [m] from crater centre. Printed symbol looks like d_tr; derivation implies D_tr.

parameters.label: Grubość wyrzutów (program)
parameters.notes: D_tc, r [m]. Lower bound (no bulking, no entrainment). Reported only outside final rim. For E < 200 Mt the deposit is limited to r < fireball radius ('blocked by atmosphere').

parameters.label: Czas dotarcia wyrzutów (balistyka)
parameters.value: T_e = (2 a^1.5 / sqrt(g_E R_E^2)) [ 2 atan( sqrt((1 - e)/(1 + e)) tan(Delta/4) ) - e sqrt(1 - e^2) sin(Delta/2) / (1 + e cos(Delta/2)) ]
parameters.notes: All ejecta from one point at 45 deg; no atmosphere, no rotation. Valid v_e^2/(g_E R_E) <= 1 (r < ~10,000 km). If T_e > 1 h the program reports fallout dominated by condensed vapour.

parameters.label: Mimośród trajektorii wyrzutu
parameters.notes: e is taken NEGATIVE when v_e^2/(g_E R_E) <= 1 (always within validity range).

parameters.label: Prędkość wyrzutu dla zasięgu
parameters.notes: Delta = r/R_E [rad].

parameters.label: Średnia wielkość fragmentów
parameters.notes: D_fr in KM, r_km in KM, d in m. Neglects terrestrial atmosphere/wind; not computed for r < 2 crater radii (paper) although Purdue code computes it everywhere.

parameters.label: Nadciśnienie (wybuch przypowierzchniowy)
parameters.method: empirical fit:1 kt surface burst (Glasstone & Dolan 1977 Fig. 3.66) + yield scaling
parameters.notes: r1 [m] scaled distance (Eq. 57); p_x = 75000 Pa, r_x = 290 m (crossover 1/r^2.3 -> 1/r). In Mach region of airbursts r_x = 289 + 0.65 z_b1 (text; code 290 + 0.65 z_b1). Uniform atmosphere, flat Earth. Paper p. 831: agrees with Zahnle 1990/Toon et al. 1994 in 1-10,000 Mt but 'probably overestimates the blast wave effects by a factor of 2-5' above 10^4 Mt (text says 'Equation 44', evidently Eq. 54). Chicxulub-scale energies (~1e8 Mt) are outside the calibrated range.

parameters.label: Nadciśnienie, odbicie regularne (2005)
parameters.notes: Superseded for the web program by Collins et al. 2017 Eq. 7.

parameters.label: Parametr p0(z_b) (2005)
parameters.notes: z_b [m] (1-kt scaled burst altitude). Superseded 2017.

parameters.label: Parametr beta(z_b) (2005)
parameters.notes: Superseded 2017.

parameters.label: Nadciśnienie, odbicie regularne (2017)
parameters.method: empirical fit:nuclear tests over wider altitude range
parameters.notes: r, z_b [m] for a 1 kt explosion (i.e. r1, z_b1 after yield scaling). Replaces Eqs. 55-56. Implemented in Purdue code (regular-reflection branch, with an undocumented linear blend of half-width 0.00328 z_b1^2 m around r_m1).

parameters.label: Odległość skalowana (1 kt)
parameters.notes: E_kt = E/4.18e12 J (paper Mt value; Purdue code uses 4.186e12). Since Collins et al. 2017 the airblast energy is max(impact energy at ground, kinetic energy lost in atmosphere).

parameters.label: Początek strefy Macha
parameters.notes: Surface burst: r_m1 = 0 (Mach region everywhere). z_b1 > 550 m: no Mach region.

parameters.label: Prędkość wiatru za frontem
parameters.notes: P0 = 1e5 Pa (1 bar); c0 ~ 330 m s^-1; p [Pa]. Exact for a perfect diatomic gas; real-gas effects at very strong shocks ignored.

parameters.label: Czas dotarcia fali (całka)
parameters.notes: Equation numbers 60-61 do not exist in the paper.

parameters.label: Prędkość fali uderzeniowej
parameters.notes: Not used by the program.

parameters.label: Czas dotarcia fali (program)
parameters.notes: c0 = 330 m s^-1 (calculator code). Large error only near the crater. Purdue code: T_b = sqrt(r^2 + z_b^2)/c0 with z_b >= 0; Imperial server reproduced only with the unclamped (negative) z_b.

parameters.label: Pęd i moment pędu impaktu
parameters.value: M_i = m_i v_i;  Gamma_i = m_i v_i R_E cos(theta)
parameters.unit: kg m s^-1; kg m^2 s^-1
parameters.notes: Compared with M_E = m_E v_E (m_E = 5.83e24 kg as printed - modern value 5.97e24; v_E = 29.78 km/s) and Gamma_E = 5.86e33 kg m^2 s^-1 (printed unit 'kg m3 s-1' is a typo).

parameters.label: Zmiana długości doby
parameters.value: Delta_T_E = (5 / (4 pi R_E)) (m_i / M_E) cos(theta) v_i T_E^2
parameters.method: angular momentum conservation, I_E = 0.4 M_E R_E^2
parameters.notes: Upper bound (equatorial impact in equatorial plane). Non-peer-reviewed note. Purdue page shows 'up to 1.50 ms' for case A.

parameters.label: Maks. amplituda fali brzeżnej tsunami
parameters.value: A_rw_max = min(D_tc/14.1, H_w)  at  R_rw = 3 D_tc / 4
parameters.notes: D_tc = transient crater in the water layer; H_w = water depth (constant along path assumed). Rim wave always generated. Non-peer-reviewed.

parameters.label: Zanik fali brzeżnej
parameters.value: A_rw = A_rw_max (R_rw / r)  for r > R_rw
parameters.notes: Inside R_rw: 'within wave-generation zone'.

parameters.label: Maks. amplituda fali zapadania
parameters.value: A_cw_max = 0.06 min(d_tc, H_w)  at  R_cw = 5 D_tc / 2;  d_tc = D_tc/2.828
parameters.notes: Only if H_w > 2 L.

parameters.label: Zanik fali zapadania
parameters.value: A_cw = A_cw_max (R_cw / r)^q,  q = 3 exp(-0.8 L/H_w)  (L/H_w < 0.5)

parameters.label: Czas dotarcia tsunami (min.)
parameters.value: T_w_min = r / min( sqrt(1.56 D_tc (1 + 39.5 (A/D_tc)^2)), sqrt(9.8 H_w) (1 + A/(2 H_w)) )
parameters.method: finite-amplitude gravity-wave speed limits, lambda = D_tc
parameters.notes: 1.56 = g/(2 pi) with g = 9.8. Note: Eq. (20) of the note has 2 pi^2 A^2/lambda^2 (=19.7 (A/lambda)^2) but Eq. (21) uses 39.5 - internal factor-2 inconsistency.

parameters.label: Czas dotarcia tsunami (maks.)
parameters.value: T_w_max = r / sqrt(1.56 D_tc tanh(6.28 H_w / D_tc))

parameters.label: Przyspieszenie grawitacyjne
parameters.locator: not stated numerically in paper; Purdue code u=9.8
parameters.notes: Paper uses symbol g_E only. Errata note tsunami eqs use 9.8.

parameters.label: Promień Ziemi
parameters.locator: not stated numerically in paper; Purdue code c=6370 km (also 637e4 m in ejecta)
parameters.notes: Imperial server map radii are consistent with 6371 km (inferred).

parameters.label: Ciśnienie atmosferyczne
parameters.notes: 1 bar.

parameters.label: Współczynnik oporu (woda)
parameters.notes: Rigid sphere, supersonic (Landau & Lifshitz 1959).

parameters.label: Czynnik naleśnikowy
parameters.notes: Physically 2-4 (Ivanov et al. 1997); 5-10 fit Tunguska (Chyba et al. 1993).

parameters.label: Wydajność świetlna
parameters.notes: Range 1e-4 to 1e-2 (Ortiz et al. 2000); velocity dependence ignored.

parameters.label: Temperatura przezroczystości
parameters.notes: Air 2000-3000 K (Nemtchinov et al. 1998); silicate vapour ~6000 K.

parameters.label: Wydajność sejsmiczna
parameters.notes: Range 1e-5 to 1e-3 (Schultz & Gault 1975).

parameters.label: Odległość punktu przegięcia (1 kt)
parameters.notes: Mach region: 289 + 0.65 z_b (text) / 290 + 0.65 z_b1 (code).

parameters.label: Średnica przejścia prosty–złożony
parameters.notes: Complex if D_tc > 2560 m.

parameters.label: Energia właściwa topnienia (granit)
parameters.notes: Pierazzo et al. 1997.

parameters.label: Megatona TNT
parameters.notes: Purdue code uses 4.186e15 J; Imperial server ~4.18e15 (inferred from 'energy lost' printout).

parameters.label: Gęstość celu: skały krystaliczne
parameters.notes: Imperial server uses 2700 (observed 2026-10-04); Purdue code 2750.

parameters.label: Gęstość dna morskiego
parameters.notes: Purdue code uses 2750 for the seafloor crater.

thresholds.notes: Scale with impact energy: Phi_ignition(E) = value * E_Mt^(1/6) (Eq. 39). Data from Glasstone & Dolan 1977 pp. 287-289 (nuclear tests).

thresholds.notes: Scale with impact energy: Phi_ignition(E) = value * E_Mt^(1/6) (Eq. 39). Data from Glasstone & Dolan 1977 pp. 287-289 (nuclear tests).

thresholds.notes: Scale with impact energy: Phi_ignition(E) = value * E_Mt^(1/6) (Eq. 39). Data from Glasstone & Dolan 1977 pp. 287-289 (nuclear tests).

thresholds.notes: Scale with impact energy: Phi_ignition(E) = value * E_Mt^(1/6) (Eq. 39). Data from Glasstone & Dolan 1977 pp. 287-289 (nuclear tests).

thresholds.notes: Scale with impact energy: Phi_ignition(E) = value * E_Mt^(1/6) (Eq. 39). Data from Glasstone & Dolan 1977 pp. 287-289 (nuclear tests).

thresholds.notes: Scale with impact energy: Phi_ignition(E) = value * E_Mt^(1/6) (Eq. 39). Data from Glasstone & Dolan 1977 pp. 287-289 (nuclear tests).

thresholds.notes: Scale with impact energy: Phi_ignition(E) = value * E_Mt^(1/6) (Eq. 39). Data from Glasstone & Dolan 1977 pp. 287-289 (nuclear tests).

thresholds.notes: Scale with impact energy: Phi_ignition(E) = value * E_Mt^(1/6) (Eq. 39). Data from Glasstone & Dolan 1977 pp. 287-289 (nuclear tests).

thresholds.effect: Cars and trucks largely displaced and grossly distorted; require rebuilding
thresholds.notes: Distance from a 1 kt explosion d1 = 126 m (scale by E_kt^(1/3)). Data from Glasstone & Dolan 1977. Purdue code mislabels the 22900 Pa threshold as 'steel-framed buildings ... incipient collapse'.
Distance from a 1 kt explosion d1 = 133 m (scale by E_kt^(1/3)). Data from Glasstone & Dolan 1977. Purdue code mislabels the 22900 Pa threshold as 'steel-framed buildings ... incipient collapse'.

thresholds.effect: Cars and trucks overturned and displaced, major repairs
thresholds.notes: Distance from a 1 kt explosion d1 = 149 m (scale by E_kt^(1/3)). Data from Glasstone & Dolan 1977. Purdue code mislabels the 22900 Pa threshold as 'steel-framed buildings ... incipient collapse'.

thresholds.effect: Multistory steel-framed office buildings: extreme frame distortion, incipient collapse
thresholds.notes: Distance from a 1 kt explosion d1 = 155 m (scale by E_kt^(1/3)). Data from Glasstone & Dolan 1977. Purdue code mislabels the 22900 Pa threshold as 'steel-framed buildings ... incipient collapse'.

disagreements.topic: Airblast for crater-forming impacts: Imperial server vs Purdue app vs paper
disagreements.sideA: Paper (p. 830: burst altitude 'is either zero for impacts where a crater is formed') and Purdue code (clamps z_b<0 to 0): surface burst, Eq. 54 with r_x=290 m, T_b=r/c0. Case A @1000 km: 101,901 Pa, 175.5 m/s, 3030 s.
disagreements.sideB: Imperial server output (2026-10-04) for the same inputs: 93,467 Pa, 164.2 m/s, 3038 s; case C: 52,855 Pa vs 89,488 Pa. Reproduced to <1e-5 (8 probes) only if the UNCLAMPED negative airburst altitude z_b from Eq. 18 (A: -75.3 km; C: -39.6 km) is used both in r_x = 290 + 0.65 z_b1 and in the slant range sqrt(r^2+z_b^2) for arrival time.
disagreements.notes: Mechanism is INFERRED by reverse engineering (exact match at 8 input combinations), not documented. Physically a negative burst altitude has no meaning; treat Imperial airblast values for crater-forming impacts as an implementation artefact. Effect grows when |z_b1| is a large fraction of 290 m (smaller impacts).

disagreements.sideB: Same paper (p. 831): uniform atmosphere and flat Earth invalid for large impacts; 'probably overestimates the blast wave effects by a factor of 2-5' above 10^4 Mt (comparison with Zahnle 1990 / Toon et al. 1994; those papers not opened here). Table 6 of the paper itself gives 77 bar at 200 km for an 18-km impactor whereas Eq. 54 gives ~131 bar.
disagreements.notes: For ~1e8 Mt use EIEP airblast only as an order-of-magnitude upper bound.

disagreements.sideA: Paper Eq. 12: I_f = 4.07 C_D H Y_i/(rho_i L0 v^2 sin theta).
disagreements.sideB: Purdue code: I_f = 2.7185 * [3 rho0 C_D H/(4 rho_i L0 sin theta)] * Y_i/v^2, i.e. effective coefficient 2.039 (half). Imperial server: for L=100 m, rho=8000, v=15 km/s, theta=90 it prints z* = 12,093 m vs 12,142 m (paper I_f) and 12,167 m (Purdue I_f) - matches neither.
disagreements.notes: Irrelevant for km-scale impactors (I_f ~1e-6, z* identical to 1 m) but matters for small strong bodies. One probe (50 m iron, 12 km/s, 90 deg) crashed the Imperial server (HTTP 500).

disagreements.sideA: Paper Eq. 3: T_RE = 109 E_Mt^0.78 (case A: 1.35e8 yr).
disagreements.sideB: Both calculators print 1.1e8 yr for case A; Purdue code: max(piecewise power law in impactor mass, 110 E_Mt^0.77).
disagreements.notes: Source of the updated law not documented on the calculator pages (not pursued; irrelevant to the 24-h simulation).

disagreements.sideB: Imperial server: 2700 kg/m3 (prints 'Target Density 2700' for Crystalline Rock).
2013 errata note: d_fr = 0.294 D_fr^0.301 km (lunar, gravity-scaled); ~74% of the old value; used by both calculators.

disagreements.sideA: Printed 2005: T_RL = (T_RE/2)(1 - cos Delta). Errata 2013: T_RL = T_RE/(2(1 - cos Delta)).
disagreements.sideB: Spherical-cap area fraction (1 - cos Delta)/2 implies T_RL = 2 T_RE/(1 - cos Delta).
disagreements.notes: Elementary geometry (no external source needed); both printed forms appear wrong by factors of 4. Not used in the simulation.

disagreements.topic: Paper Table 6 vs paper equations (18-km impactor at 200 km)
disagreements.sideA: Table 6 (2005 program output): ejecta thickness 137 m; peak overpressure 77 bar; wind 2220 m/s.
disagreements.sideB: Eqs. 47 and 54 as printed (independent implementation): 117 m; 131 bar; 2900 m/s. Other Table 6 entries (E, D_fr = 186 km, R_f = 236 km, M = 10.4, T_e = 206 s, 1.75-km and 40-m cases incl. 0.80 bar/145 m/s and 0.004 bar/0.96 m/s) are reproduced.
disagreements.notes: Unexplained; possibly a different implementation detail in the 2005 code. Current calculators follow the printed equations.

openQuestions: Imperial server airblast: confirm with the authors (G. S. Collins) whether using the negative airburst altitude for crater-forming impacts is intended; until then prefer the paper/Purdue surface-burst values.
Imperial server entry model for small strong impactors (z* = 12,093 m for L=100 m iron, 15 km/s, vertical) matches neither Eq. 11/12 as printed nor the Purdue code; server source code is not public.

Imperial server (distance-only mode) prints no thermal, seismic or ejecta values; only map radii are available, so the oracle for those keys rests on the Purdue client code (verified against the live Purdue page).
Paper Table 6 values for the 18-km (Chicxulub-like) case (ejecta 137 m, 77 bar at 200 km) are not reproduced by the printed Eqs. 47/54 (117 m, 131 bar) - origin unknown.

EIEP validity for Chicxulub scale: entry model is stated for impactors < 1 km (p. 820); airblast overestimated 2-5x above 1e4 Mt; ejecta ignores atmosphere/rotation and condensed-vapour (spherule) fallout; thermal model ignores ejecta re-entry heating (global wildfire mechanism discussed qualitatively only). These need dedicated threads (re-entry radiation, spherule layer, global tsunami).
